title: stream-sanitizer: unify CFG+regex constraint serialization and fix tokenizer edge-case framing
author: Liam O'Connor
description:
Motivation: Streaming structured outputs that must satisfy grammar/CFG or regex constraints are fragile in two common scenarios: (1) tokenizers that split constraint boundaries across byte/word pieces (BPE, SentencePiece) cause frame breaks and invalid partial outputs during streaming, leading to downstream toolcall parsing failures; (2) combined constraint backends (CFG + regex) produce conflicting accept/reject decisions at stream boundaries when the serializer does eager framing. This PR introduces a "stream sanitizer" layer in the OpenAI-compat and runtime constraint pipeline to make streaming+constraints robust for tool/function-calling and structured output.

What this change does (single-pass summary):
- Adds a serializer+sanitizer component that sits between the constrained-decoder and the streaming encoder. The sanitizer buffers a minimal lookahead window (configurable per model/codec) to ensure emitted frames never split tokenizer atoms required by active constraints.
- Introduces a unified constraint-resolution pass: CFG rules and regex predicates are translated to a shared edge grammar that reports stable/unstable token prefixes rather than binary accept/reject on the fly. This avoids flip-flopping during streaming when partial tokens match multiple alternatives.
- Implements tokenizer-aware boundary heuristics for common tokenizers (gpt-bpe, spm, unigram): the sanitizer uses tokenizer metadata (token byte-length, continuation flags) to prefer emission only at safe split points or to add escape markers when necessary for OpenAI-compat streaming framing.
- Adds a fallback serializer that emits a safe "continuation marker" token sequence (configurable) when lookahead would exceed latency SLOs; consumer-side parsers (OpenAI-compat shim) know how to drop the marker and resume parsing. This reduces tail latency regressions while preserving correctness.
- Wire changes across modules: runtime constraint orchestrator, openai-compat streaming shim, console evens, and SDK streaming clients (TS) include decoder hints so clients can parse streamed structured outputs deterministically.

Why this is different from previous constraint fixes: earlier PRs fixed token-boundary heuristics or improved CFG backends in isolation. This PR focuses on the serialization boundary and the interoperability between grammar/reg-ex constraints and the byte/token framing used for streaming and toolcalls. It is intended to reduce production parsing incidents (see SUP-1337) and improve developer experience for function/tool-calling.

Testing and validation:
- End-to-end regression harness added for 5 representative models (gpt-bpe small/med, spm-legacy, spm-new, unigram) that runs 1200 streaming episodes with combinations of CFG-only, regex-only, and CFG+regex constraints. No parser failures observed in 100k streamed frames; baseline had ~0.8% parse failure for mixed constraints.
- Performance microbenchmarks: median additional latency per request +2.8ms for short responses (<64 tokens) and +0.9ms for long responses (>=512 tokens) with default lookahead=6. Cost/throughput impact measured on ded-cpu and ded-gpu pools; results acceptable for Dedicated customers and opt-in for Hosted.
- Unit tests: sanitizer heuristics, tokenizer metadata mapping, fallback marker round-trip, and OpenAI-compat client parsing updated. Integration tests added to redwood-e2e harness.

Operational notes and rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag "stream_sanitizer_v1" and OpenAI-compat config "sanitize_streaming_frames". Default enabled for dedicated instances and opt-in for hosted.
- Console rollout plan: start with 5% of hosted traffic (non-prod) for 48 hours, track parser error rate and tail latency. See ENG-4821 for rollout checklist.

Backward compatibility: Client SDKs that do not understand the continuation marker will still receive valid text; the marker is chosen to be a rare, non-printing control sequence and sanitized by SDKs. However, the PR adds an opt-in compatibility header that SDKs should include to guarantee correct parsing; older SDKs will fall back to non-sanitized streaming behavior.

Files changed (high level): updated runtime/constraint orchestrator, openai-compat/streaming shim, redwood-sdk-typescript streaming client, e2e tests, docs/structured-output.md.

Merge outcome: squash-merged. Release notes appended.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Nice design. Two main asks: (1) make lookahead window configurable per-model in addition to global, (2) add a CI job that runs the e2e harness on the smallest dedicated GPU to catch allocation regressions. Please address in follow-up or here.

Miguel Torres: Found a race in the pooled buffer deallocation when an error path triggers early. Suggested using a scoped buffer object. Also asked for more comments explaining the continuation marker contract so infra teams don't misinterpret as an escape sequence. Fixed in commit 7c9b3d0.

Evelyn Kim: Approved after small test additions. Left a nit about doc wording for SDK compat header.
Author reply: addressed Asha's per-model config request (added model_profiles table) and Miguel's buffer race; updated docs per Evelyn's nit.
release_notes: Structured-output: added streaming sanitizer to prevent tokenizer-boundary and combined-constraint parsing failures. Default gated; opt-in for hosted. Improves tool/function-calling stability under constrained decoders. See docs/structured-output.md for migration steps and SDK updates.
notes_for_ops: Rollout using feature flag stream_sanitizer_v1; monitor parser_error_rate, stream_frame_retries, and p99 latency. If regressions, toggle off or reduce lookahead per model. See ENG-4821 for rollback steps.
